tech.name: DeepSeek Super-agent (dsh-superagent)
tech.one_line: One router agent takes requests from team chat and GitHub and hands each to its own worker agent, running many at once.

hook.text: Watching one AI helper is easy; watching ten is not.

before.text: A person drives each coding-agent session step by step and can supervise only a few at once.

claims.text: DeepSeek's team estimates a person can supervise only 3-5 active agent sessions at once.

new.text: A router (main Session) listens to GitHub and team chat, turns allowed requests into tickets, and gives each ticket its own worker session and directory; tickets run concurrently.

claims.text: Listens to GitHub and optionally Feishu; answers in the original conversation, e.g. with a pull request.
The main Session evaluates events, accepts and dispatches Tickets, and replies (orchestrator, preset dsh-superagent-router).
Each Ticket gets its own Executor Session worker-<id> and its own directory; launches run concurrently up to a slot limit.
It stays quiet while it works and writes again when a result is ready.

why.text: Human attention is the limit, so the agent speaks only when a person must act or can use a result.

claims.text: Core principle: take as little human attention as possible; speak only when a person must act or can use a result.

how.text: Open-source research prototype for one GitHub repo; ask your coding agent to read SETUP.md and set it up with you.

claims.text: Research prototype, not an official DeepSeek product; MIT; for one GitHub repository; setup by asking a coding agent to read SETUP.md.

outro.text: Next: what a coding-agent session is.
